inputs.original_text: Workers employed in the support programmes of the Ministry of Education, Sport and Youth staged a protest outside the Presidential Palace on Thursday and announced a 24-hour strike, calling for legally binding job security guarantees — even as the government argued it had already delivered on the most significant demands. At the heart of the [...]
inputs.modified_text: A 24-hour strike over job guarantees shows how little power workers have when stable employment is still uncertain: they have to disrupt education just to make their security impossible to ignore. The government saying it has met the most significant demands is not enough if workers still cannot count on secure jobs. Families need education, and that means respecting the people who provide it—not treating their labor action as the source of instability. The government should negotiate guarantees that workers can trust.
